title: First-Order Linear Ordinary Differential Equations
content: A first-order linear ODE has the standard form dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x). It is solved using the Integrating Factor I(x) = exp(integral(P(x) dx)). Multiplying the entire equation by I(x) condenses the left-hand side into the exact derivative d/dx [y * I(x)] = Q(x) * I(x), which integrates directly to y * I(x) = integral(Q(x) * I(x) dx) + C.

title: Definition and Properties of the Laplace Transform
content: The one-sided Laplace Transform of a function f(t) defined for t >= 0 is given by L{f(t)} = F(s) = integral from 0 to infinity of e^(-st) * f(t) dt. Key elementary transforms include L{1} = 1/s, L{e^(at)} = 1/(s - a) for s > a, and L{t^n} = n! / s^(n+1). For derivatives, L{f'(t)} = s * F(s) - f(0), which transforms differential equations into algebraic equations.

title: Fourier Series Representation of Periodic Functions
content: A periodic function f(x) with period 2L satisfying Dirichlet conditions can be expanded as f(x) = a0/2 + sum_{n=1}^inf [an * cos(n*pi*x/L) + bn * sin(n*pi*x/L)]. The Euler-Fourier coefficients are: an = (1/L) * integral_{-L}^L f(x) * cos(n*pi*x/L) dx, and bn = (1/L) * integral_{-L}^L f(x) * sin(n*pi*x/L) dx. For an even function, bn = 0; for an odd function, an = 0 and a0 = 0.

title: Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors, and Characteristic Equations
content: For a square n x n matrix A, a scalar lambda is an eigenvalue and non-zero vector v is an eigenvector if A * v = lambda * v. This is equivalent to (A - lambda * I) * v = 0. Non-trivial solutions exist if and only if det(A - lambda * I) = 0, which is the characteristic polynomial of degree n. The sum of eigenvalues equals the trace of A, and their product equals det(A).
